Where it began

Herschelle Gibbs was born in Green Point on 23 February 1974, and he was the kind of schoolboy who was good at everything. He went to St Joseph's Marist College before moving to Diocesan College in Rondebosch, and he played for South African Schools teams at rugby, cricket and football.

At Diocesan College he was in the first rugby XV with three boys who went on to become Springboks, and he played Craven Week for Western Province in 1992 alongside Percy Montgomery. Cricket won in the end, and rugby's loss was cricket's gain.

The player

He played 90 Tests between 1996 and 2008, scoring 6,167 runs at 41.95 with 14 hundreds and 26 fifties. His highest score was 228 against Pakistan at Newlands, which came off just 240 balls. His other double hundred, 211 not out against New Zealand in 1999, took 468 balls, so he could do patience as well as fireworks.

With Graeme Smith he formed one of the great opening pairs. They put on 368 in that Newlands Test, a South African record, and they became the first pair in Test history to pass 300 together three times. He also shared an unbeaten stand of 315 with Jacques Kallis for the second wicket.

What made him special

He had a rare gift for timing, and the one-day game showed it best. On 12 March 2006, in the highest-scoring one-day match there had ever been, he made 175 from 111 balls to lead South Africa to victory over Australia. He reached his hundred in 79, and scored 126 of his runs in boundaries. At the 2007 World Cup, against the Netherlands, he struck all six balls of a Daan van Bunge over for six, the first man to do so in a one-day international.

He was also a brilliant fielder, quick to the ball and deadly with a run-out. There were spells when the runs dried up, and he fell in the nineties more often than he would have liked, but when he was in form there were few more thrilling sights in the game.

Away from the middle

After Tests he played Twenty20 cricket all over the world: for Glamorgan and Yorkshire in England, Deccan Chargers and Mumbai Indians in the IPL, and Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash, where he helped them reach the final. He went on to coach, leading the Rotterdam Rhinos, the Colombo Kings and, from January 2021, the Karachi Kings, and he had also worked with Kuwait's national team.

And finally

Those six sixes did more than make history. Through a competition run by the tournament's sponsor, they raised a million US dollars for Habitat for Humanity's housing projects. Very few overs in cricket have done as much good.
